content:
Apple is working on a major redesigned MacBook Pro (possibly called MacBook Ultra), expected to launch in October. Here are three rumored new features we've been waiting a long time for.

#1: OLED Display

When it comes to a product that many users stare at all day, it's hard to overstate the value of display technology. Yet for years, the Mac has lagged behind Apple's other products in adopting the most cutting-edge display technology.

OLED has been the mainstay of the iPhone for years, and the iPad Pro also introduced tandem OLED in 2024, which many Mac users have been eagerly awaiting. Now the new MacBook Pro is finally bringing OLED to the Mac.

The new MacBook Pro with OLED is expected to deliver purer blacks, better contrast, and hopefully improved battery life. Hopefully it can match the excellent tandem OLED found in the iPad.

#2: Touchscreen

Apple has long insisted that the Mac doesn't need a touchscreen, despite virtually all of its competitors' products supporting touch. But rumors suggest we'll finally see the first Mac with touch support.

The new MacBook Pro will feature a touchscreen, and macOS 27 is already filled with hints of this feature. Further software optimizations are expected to make touch operations feel more natural on Mac.

Although touch functionality is being added, macOS will still primarily be designed for trackpad and keyboard operation. Touch will be a supplementary tool for the Mac, not a replacement for traditional input methods, providing a complement for users accustomed to touch on iPhone, iPad, and computers.

#3: Farewell to the 'Notch'

When Apple last redesigned the MacBook Pro in 2021, it added the 'notch' design, which originally appeared on the iPhone. The 'notch' later expanded to the MacBook Air, becoming a hallmark of contemporary Mac design.

Top comment posted by scottishwildcat

Of course I haven't been waiting for any of the above. Laptops don't need OLED, anyone who touches my screen with their fingers will get it, and the 'notch' has never been a problem at all.

But reports indicate the new MacBook Pro will abandon the 'notch' in favor of a punch-hole camera cutout, looking similar to the design we've seen on the iPhone Duo.

Dynamic Island will also be ported to macOS, allowing the camera cutout to blend seamlessly on the Mac just like on the iPhone. As someone who finds the 'notch' more obtrusive on the Mac than on the iPhone, I'm looking forward to the 'notch' finally disappearing.

Will you upgrade to the new MacBook Pro? Why or why not? Leave a comment and let us know.
